ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6516, as amended); Act on Regulation and Punishment of Concealment of Criminal Proceeds (Act No. 15692, as amended); Act on Prohibition of Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction (Act No. 14819, as amended); Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information; Financial Services Commission Regulations on Identification of Beneficial Owners and Customer Due Diligence; Supreme Court Commercial Registration Rules.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Commercial Registry Office, Seoul Central District Court
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path: notarize the certified registry extract before a Korean notary public, then request an Apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for use in any Hague Apostille Convention member state. Consular path for non-member states: notarization followed by MOFA authentication and consular legalization at the destination-state consulate in Seoul. The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive; Apostille and consular legalization must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea, Internet Registration Office (IROS) and competent District Court Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path: notarize the certified certificate of existence issued by the Korean court registry and obtain an Apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Consular path: notarized certificate is authenticated by MOFA and then legalized by the consulate of the destination jurisdiction; no Apostille is used. The routes are exclusive alternatives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Notarized Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Yuhan Hoesa and a Korean Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path: execute the board resolution and power of attorney, notarize the signature before a Korean notary public, and obtain an Apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Consular path: after notarization, MOFA authentication and consular legalization by the destination-state consulate; never combine Apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Notary Public and District Court Commercial Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path: notarize the certified copy of the Articles of Association and request an Apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Consular path: notarized copy is authenticated by MOFA and legalized by the relevant foreign consulate in Seoul for a non-Apostille jurisdiction. The two authentication mechanisms are mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Domestic Korean commercial bank (Shinhan, KB Kookmin, Woori, or Hana Bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path: have the bank letter notarized by a Korean notary public and obtain an Apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Consular path: notarized letter is authenticated by MOFA and then legalized by the destination-state consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are separate, non-sequential alternatives.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every proposed director, shareholder, UBO, and authorized signatory must be screened before name clearance against the UN Consolidated Security Council Sanctions Lists and UNSCR 1373 and 2253 designations, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, the European Union consolidated financial sanctions lists, and the Republic of Korea domestic designations administered by the Financial Services Commission and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. PEPs must be identified using an FATF-compliant database covering domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, immediate family members, and close associates; any PEP match requires enhanced due diligence, documented source of wealth, and senior-management approval prior to incorporation or bank onboarding. Screening must be repeated at account opening and within thirty days after any change in ownership or control.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IROS; iros.go.kr) - Company Name Search and Reservation Module, operated by the Supreme Court Registry Office
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory name must be in Korean Hangul and must show four tiers: (1) distinctive trade symbol; (2) optional phonetic transliteration of a foreign brand; (3) a business-objective descriptor corresponding to ISIC/KSIC 7490; (4) the mandatory legal-form suffix Yuhan Hoesa or Jusik Hoesa. A parallel English name may be reserved as a secondary transliteration, but the Hangul name controls registry priority; words of foreign origin must be rendered in Hangul phonetically and, where possible confusion exists, a substantiated phonetic equivalence table must be attached.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant is notified with a coded reason. Within fourteen days, an applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the head of the district court registry office, setting out grounds and rebuttals, together with a new name-check report and transliteration certificate. If the refusal is based on a ministerial restriction token, the applicant must obtain written pre-approval from the relevant Minister and resubmit via IROS. A one-time 30-day extension may be requested before reservation expires. An administrative lawsuit may be filed in the competent Administrative District Court within 90 days of the final rejection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Commercial registration under the Korean Commercial Act requires a fixed physical address with actual leasehold interest within the registry district. For a professional multilingual translation and media dubbing business, the National Tax Service and domestic banks will reject a mere commercial mailbox or virtual office because it cannot verify a place for employees, documents, and equipment in an unscheduled inspection. Remote-working studios are permitted only if a managed office lease, utility contract, and service-provider agreement are maintained on site.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (i) registered office signboard; (ii) lease agreement in the company's name; (iii) utility bills for the last three months; (iv) physical workspace or dubbing studio equipment; (v) tax invoices, accounting ledgers, and client contracts; (vi) employment records. Quantified risk of unannounced inspection by the National Tax Service local tax office or the district court registry within the first operating year: 12% for a dedicated brick-and-mortar office; 25% if the registered address is a coworking, virtual-office, or serviced mailbox without dedicated workspace. For a low-risk localization agency with ISIC 7490, the expected annual inspection probability after year one is 8%.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), particularly Articles 287-287-42 (Limited Liability Company, Yuhan Hoesa) and Article 288 (Articles of Incorporation), Article 289 (Subscription of Shares), Article 290 (Payment of Contributions), Article 291 (Registration of Incorporation), and Article 292 (Effect of Registration).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Local District Court Registry Office (Beopwonsa) under the Supreme Court of Korea, specifically the Registration Division of the court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office address.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Jeong-gwan) duly notarized by a notary public, accompanied by the Application for Corporation Registration (Beobin Deunggi Sinsaek) and supporting documents.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Commercial Act does not impose a minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa. However, the total amount of contributions must be fully paid in at the time of incorporation, and the paid-in capital must be deposited into a bank account in the name of the company (or a designated escrow account) until the registration is completed. The deposit certificate must be submitted to the registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] (YUHAN HOESA) ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT IN LIEU OF A MEETING ON [DATE] AT [TIME] AT THE REGISTERED OFFICE OF THE COMPANY. WHEREAS, the Company was incorporated under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea on [DATE] and has received its Certificate of Incorporation; WHEREAS, the Board of Directors is authorized to take all actions necessary to commence business operations, including the subscription of share capital, the establishment of banking relationships, the adoption of a registered office, and the appointment of statutory officers; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The Board hereby ratifies and confirms the subscription of the entire issued share capital of the Company, consisting of [NUMBER] shares of KRW [AMOUNT] each, fully paid in cash, as set forth in the Articles of Incorporation. The Board authorizes the Chief Executive Officer to execute any documents and take any steps necessary to evidence the payment of such capital and to obtain the required deposit certificate from the bank. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Board hereby designates [BANK NAME] with branch at [ADDRESS] as the primary banking institution of the Company. The Board authorizes the opening of corporate bank accounts, including a general operating account and a payroll account, and appoints the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer as joint signatories for all banking transactions, with the authority to execute any account agreements, mandates, and related instruments. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The Board adopts the registered office of the Company at [FULL ADDRESS], which shall be the legal seat of the Company for all statutory and administrative purposes. The Board authorizes the Chief Executive Officer to execute any lease or service agreements and to file any notices with the competent registry as required by law. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: The Board appoints [NAME] as Chief Executive Officer, [NAME] as Chief Financial Officer, and [NAME] as Company Secretary, each to serve until their successors are duly elected. The Board authorizes the Company Secretary to prepare and file all statutory returns, to maintain the corporate records, and to act as the point of contact for regulatory authorities. 5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION: The Board authorizes any officer of the Company to execute, deliver, and file all documents, instruments, and certificates necessary to carry out the foregoing resolutions, and to take all such actions as may be required to give full effect to these resolutions. This resolution shall be effective immediately and shall remain in full force until revoked or amended by a subsequent resolution of the Board. ADOPTED this [DATE] by the unanimous written consent of the Board of Directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (Beopmub) and the local Court Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in Korean, including the company name (Yuhan Hoesa), purpose (professional multilingual translation and media dubbing services), registered office address, total authorized shares, par value, and the names and contributions of each founding member. The document must be signed by all incorporators and then notarized by a licensed notary public. The notary will verify the identity of the signatories and the legality of the provisions. After notarization, obtain a certified copy of the notarized Articles. Ensure that the company name is not identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names by conducting a preliminary name search on the Supreme Court's registry portal (IROS).
required_dossiers: Identification documents (passport or resident registration card) of all incorporators
Power of attorney if any incorporator is represented
Proof of payment of notary fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry rejects the name or the Articles, correct the deficiencies and re-notarize. If the name is rejected, select an alternative name and re-submit. If the notary identifies legal issues, amend the Articles accordingly and re-execute.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Paid-in Capital and Issuance of Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate bank account in the name of the company (or a designated escrow account) at a commercial bank. Each incorporator must transfer their respective contribution to this account. The bank will issue a certificate of deposit (Yipgeumjeungmyeong) confirming the total paid-in capital. This certificate is a mandatory attachment to the incorporation application. The account must remain frozen until the company is registered, after which the funds become available for business use. Ensure that the deposit is made in full before proceeding to the next step.
required_dossiers: Bank's internal forms for deposit certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays issuance, request a written confirmation of the deposit. If any incorporator fails to pay, the incorporation process cannot proceed; the defaulting party must be replaced or the capital structure amended.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing for Incorporation with the Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Application for Corporation Incorporation (Beobin Deunggi Sinsaek) to the registry office having jurisdiction over the registered office. Attach the notarized Articles, the deposit certificate, the list of directors and auditors (if any), and the consent forms of the appointed officers. The application must be signed by the incorporators or their legal representatives. The registry will review the documents for compliance with the Commercial Act. Upon approval, the registry will issue a Certificate of Incorporation (Deunggiwonjeung) and assign a corporate registration number. The registration fee is approximately KRW 150,000 (USD 120) plus court stamp duty.
required_dossiers: List of directors and officers with their consent
Proof of payment of registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query or suspension, respond within the given deadline (usually 2 weeks) by providing additional documents or clarifications. If the application is rejected, correct the defects and re-file. Legal counsel may be engaged to expedite resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with Tax Authorities and Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) and Local District Tax Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 20 days of incorporation, file for business registration (Saeopja Deungrok) with the local district tax office. Submit the Certificate of Incorporation, the Articles, and the corporate seal certificate. The NTS will issue a Business Registration Certificate (Saeopja Deungrokjeung) and assign a corporate tax identification number. This certificate is required for opening a permanent bank account, issuing tax invoices, and conducting business. Additionally, register for value-added tax (VAT) and corporate income tax. The company must also obtain a corporate seal certificate (Injang) from the registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office requests additional information, provide it promptly. If the registration is delayed, the company may face penalties for late filing; apply for an extension if necessary. Ensure all documents are in Korean or accompanied by certified translations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Permanent Bank Account and Corporate Seal Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Bank and Local Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Business Registration Certificate, open a permanent corporate bank account with the designated bank. Provide the Business Registration Certificate, the Certificate of Incorporation, the corporate seal, and the identification of the authorized signatories. The bank will verify the corporate existence and issue a corporate bank account. Simultaneously, register the corporate seal (injang) with the registry office to obtain a seal certificate (injangjeungmyeong). This seal is used for all official documents, contracts, and banking transactions. The seal certificate is also required for opening the bank account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account opening due to incomplete documentation, rectify the missing items. If the seal registration is delayed, the company may use a notarized seal for interim transactions. Ensure the seal is registered with the same registry where the company is incorporated.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - The business scope (ISIC 7490 - Professional Multilingual Translation and Media Dubbing) is a pure professional service with no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing activities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - No industrial operating license is required for translation and dubbing services under Korean law.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - No environmental impact assessment is required as the business does not involve any physical operations, emissions, or waste generation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - The activity is classified as a non-industrial service and is not subject to the Environmental Impact Assessment Act (Act No. 14476).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - No discharge or emission thresholds apply. The company must still comply with general waste disposal regulations for office waste, but no specific industrial standards are mandated.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - The business operates in an office environment. However, the company must comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act (Act No. 16272) for general workplace safety, including fire safety measures, emergency exits, and first aid provisions. A fire safety inspection certificate from the local fire department may be required for the office premises, but this is a standard building compliance requirement, not a specific industrial license.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; statutory electronic tax portal: HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr). Export declarations and customs-related export evidence are handled by the Korea Customs Service (KCS) through UNI-PASS (unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Yuhan Hoesa must complete the Korean Business Registration procedure under the Value-Added Tax Act and the Framework Act on National Taxes before or no later than 20 days after commencing business. The LLC files the Business Registration Application with the district tax office having jurisdiction over its registered office, or electronically through NTS HomeTax. Required supporting documents include: articles of incorporation, corporate registration certificate, director identification and Korean address evidence, lease or office-occupancy documentation, a written application signed with the corporate seal or authorized electronic certificate, and, for foreign-invested LLCs, foreign shareholder and power-of-attorney records. The NTS issues a 10-digit corporate Business Registration Number, which functions as both the Corporate Taxpayer Identification Number and VAT registration number. A foreign non-resident entity that has no Korean place of business but makes Korean taxable supplies of electronic or digital services must separately register in HomeTax using the foreign business-operator registration pathway; the NTS requires a Korean tax representative, a duly notarized power of attorney, the foreign certificate of incorporation, overseas tax identification data, and evidence of Korean digital supply. If the foreign entity only holds shares in or receives payments from the Yuhan Hoesa, no separate Korean VAT ID is required, but withholding tax and corporate income tax reporting obligations apply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law does not provide a check-the-box election or a taxpayer-driven hybrid mismatch classification election. The Yuhan Hoesa is mandatorily classified as a Korean domestic corporation for Corporate Income Tax purposes and as a VAT business operator under the Value-Added Tax Act; no transparency election is available for a limited liability company.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Korean Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act, supplemented by the Local Consumption Tax Act for revenue allocation; the headline VAT rate remains 10%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary exemption threshold in Korean won applies to a domestic Yuhan Hoesa; any taxable commercial supply triggers mandatory VAT business registration from commencement of business. Foreign non-resident suppliers without a Korean fixed place of business that supply electronic or digital services to Korean recipients must likewise register from the time they commence Korean taxable supply; no general de minimis registration threshold exists in local currency. The KRW 80,000,000 simplified taxable person regime affects calculation and reporting simplification for very small domestic businesses, not exemption from registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-Tax Invoice filing through NTS HomeTax. Every taxable B2B supply, including zero-rated export services, requires an electronic tax invoice issued through the HomeTax e-Tax Invoice system or an NTS-accredited ERP/ASP connector using the Korean standard electronic tax-invoice XML schema and HomeTax authentication certificates for API-based submission. There is no real-time per-invoice government clearance before issuance, but each e-tax invoice receives an NTS verification code and is subject to full digital validation, purchaser verification through HomeTax, automatic matching with VAT returns, and anti-fraud verification-code stamping. Issuance details and correction notices must be submitted electronically according to the statutory VAT return cycle; failure to issue or transmit an e-tax invoice triggers penalty taxes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act, the export of goods from Korea and services supplied to a foreign country or foreign resident are zero-rated. For the ISIC 7490 localization business, translation, subtitling, dubbing, voice-over, media localization, linguistic QA, and related professional services qualify for 0% VAT when they are supplied under a contract with a foreign counterparty, the services are actually performed for and used outside Korea, and the consideration is paid in foreign currency and repatriated to Korea. Physical media exported by customs also qualifies if a valid KCS export declaration and transport documents exist. The taxpayer must retain the complete NTS evidentiary package set out below.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Bill of Entry) accepted by the Korea Customs Service via UNI-PASS, required for physical media and tangible deliverables; for pure digital service exports the equivalent electronic delivery evidence must be retained.
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing shipment from Korea to a foreign destination whenever physical media, masters, or localized materials are exported.
Commercial invoice and signed localization or dubbing services agreement describing the service, foreign beneficiary, and foreign-currency consideration.
Inward Remittance Certificate (Foreign Exchange Receipt Certificate) issued by a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank, showing receipt of the export proceeds from the foreign client.
Digital release and acceptance log for electronically delivered content, including delivery timestamps, file checksums, or platform acknowledgement confirming offshore use.
Foreign client's certificate of tax residence, business registration extract, or equivalent documentary proof that the recipient is not a Korean resident.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service may jointly audit export zero-ratings by matching export declarations, foreign-exchange receipts, e-tax invoices, and bank records. If the documentation bundle is incomplete or the foreign-exchange repatriation occurs after the statutory 180-day period without NTS or regulatory approval, the zero-rating is disallowed retroactively. The NTS will assess the 10% VAT on the original invoice amount, add penalty tax for unfaithful returns up to 40% of the deficient VAT in concealment or serious negligence cases, impose late-payment surcharge interest, and claw back any refund previously given with interest. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days may additionally trigger enforcement under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, and intentional fabrication of export documents is subject to criminal sanctions under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act and related statutes.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) acting jointly with the Ministry of Strategy and Finance (MOSF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations; the BOK operates the national FX reporting system, while authorized foreign exchange banks execute convertibility and settlement operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains an OECD Article VIII recognized current-account convertible regime. The Korean won is fully convertible for current transactions such as royalty payments, service fees, and dividend remittances once a foreign exchange bank confirms the underlying trade contract and purpose code. Capital-account transactions, including foreign equity injection and cross-border loans, are not prohibited by tariffs or surrender quotas but are subject to mandatory reporting/declaration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; they require either a prior filing, post-facto declaration, or in certain cases approval from MOSF or the Bank of Korea. Profit remittance hurdles are primarily documentary: the paying entity must have completed audited financial statements, a certificate of tax payment for the dividend withholding tax, a corporate seal certificate, and the foreign investor must present the foreign investment registration certificate. There is no statutory cap on remittable ordinary profits once corporate income tax, dividend tax, and settlement fees are satisfied. Export proceeds are not subject to a mandatory conversion ratio; the exporter may retain foreign currency in a foreign currency deposit at a licensed domestic bank or convert at the market rate through an authorized foreign exchange bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations, export proceeds must be received in Korea within eighteen (18) months from the date of export declaration, unless an extended settlement period is reported to the Korean customs office and the authorized foreign exchange bank. The mandatory conversion ratio in Korean won is zero percent (0%) under the fully liberalized current-account regime: exporters may retain 100% of proceeds in a foreign-currency deposit account, or sell them to the authorized bank at the prevailing market rate. If the export declaration amount exceeds USD 5,000 equivalent, the exporter must submit an Export Proceeds Settlement Confirmation to the bank in compliance with Article 17-2 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW and USD multi-currency)
Capital Escrow Account (Foreign Investment Report/Registration Account)
Basic Operational Currency Account / SWIFT payout account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low legal viability as the primary settlement rail. South Korea does not grant EU-style electronic money institution licenses; a digital EMI cannot hold Korean-won deposits or issue Korean bank account numbers under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act unless it is authorized as a small-payment agency or licensed financial company. Wise B2B and Payoneer may be used as supplementary disbursement rails for low-value localization vendor payments outside Korea, but they are not authorized to serve as the corporate bank of record, capital escrow vehicle, or FX settlement counterparty for the Yuhan Hoesa account. The entity must maintain a Tier 1 Korean commercial bank account for statutory FC/FRN reporting, FDI capital verification, tax withholding, and dividend remittance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory director(s) must in practice appear physically in the Korean bank branch to provide original passport, corporate seal registration certificate, articles of incorporation, proof of registered address, and live signature specimen. Pure remote opening is generally not permitted for a newly formed non-resident-owned Yuhan Hoesa. Some Tier 1 banks may accept a remote consular interview only if the bank's Global Compliance Committee pre-approves the consular notarization of board resolutions, uses videoconference identity confirmation, and obtains a Korean-licensed lawyer's certified true-copy opinion; however, the first account activation and signatory mandate creation still require either the director, a duly appointed local signatory, or a Korean attorney with a general power of attorney to attend in person.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds and original economic wealth for the incoming foreign equity injection and working capital transfers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a notarized source-of-wealth statement in English or Korean, six months of personal/corporate bank statements from the funding shareholder, audited financial statements of the parent holding company, evidence of accumulated profits through tax assessment letters, and a breakdown showing that the remitted amount is proportionate to the shareholder's income and assets.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Indirect or opaque beneficial ownership chain, particularly if shares are held through a Korean representative director or a non-resident intermediary.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the company register (certified extract of shareholder registry), certificate of corporate seal, articles of incorporation, board resolution approving the banking mandate, a UBO declaration form, passport copies of the 25% or more beneficial owners, and a full corporate structure chart from the ultimate natural person to the Yuhan Hoesa.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flags from cross-border invoices for translation and localization services with no underlying performance evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the complete service agreement, localized media delivery reports, translation memory/cat-tool audit logs, time-stamped proof of delivery to local distributors, invoices and payment schedules tied to identifiable projects, and a detailed profit-and-loss reconciliation showing the service margin is economically consistent with ISIC 7490 operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Historical or anticipated non-compliance with Korean FX declaration requirements, especially incorrect purpose codes on inward remittances.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide past FX transaction declarations, bank advice slips matching each purpose code, written confirmation from the tax accountant that the entity has complied with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, the Korean corporate settlement certificate, and evidence of no unresolved tax liabilities from the National Tax Service (NTS).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant route is to file the Foreign Investment Report (FDI report) with KOTRA or an authorized foreign exchange bank before the SWIFT wire is sent, using the statutory purpose-code category for foreign direct investment in equity capital. The remittance should be a telegraphic transfer from the foreign shareholder's own bank account to the bank-designated escrow/foreign-investment registration account, with the payment narrative clearly stating 'EQUITY SUBSCRIPTION - Yuhan Hoesa Capital Account' and referencing the FDI report number. After the funds are credited, the bank verifies the inflow, issues the Foreign Investment Registration Certificate, and the capital amount is booked as paid-in capital. Conversion into Korean won must occur at the authorized bank's prevailing customer spot rate; the bank maintains the required report to the Bank of Korea through the FX information system. Wires must not be split into odd amounts, and no third-party trust funds may be used without a supplemental AML declaration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for localization services should be executed via SWIFT MT103 priority remittance through the Tier 1 bank, with the correct service-fee purpose code, supporting invoices, and tax invoices attached within the bank's reporting threshold. For high-value or repeat deliveries of licensed media content, an irrevocable documentary credit (Commercial LC) can be established by the Korean buyer or the entity's foreign client; however, since ISIC 7490 is a service activity, documentary collections (D/P or D/A) are uncommon and should only be used when accompanied by a delivery confirmation certificate, a service acceptance certificate, and the underlying contract. The bank will clear outgoing Korean-won disbursements through BOK-Wire+ RTGS and foreign-currency disbursements through its SWIFT/CHIPS correspondent network; all disbursements must keep the invoice, contract, proof of service, and FX declaration number in a three-way match to avoid frozen payments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward foreign exchange contracts (KRW/USD, KRW/EUR, KRW/JPY) up to the underlying export/import or service transaction amount

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only when executed as a hedging overlay through an authorized Korean financial institution for underlying KRW exposure; direct offshore NDFs by the Korean entity are not permitted
Cross-currency swaps (KRW/USD or KRW/EUR) with a maturity not exceeding the underlying service contract term, requiring FETA disclosure and bank confirmation of the real exposure
Plain-vanilla FX options on licensed Korean banks for hedging short-duration localization receivables, subject to the bank's FX derivatives eligibility assessment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary general meeting of members and statutory approval of separate financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company record kept at the registered office in the Republic of Korea; no filing to the court registry unless the meeting resolves a registrable change such as an officer replacement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of each fiscal year; for a calendar-year entity, on or before March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct filing penalty; however, any member may request a court order to convene the meeting, and a dormant company that holds no valid meetings and conducts no business for 5 years becomes subject to court-ordered dissolution under the Korean Commercial Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent external auditor's report and audited financial statements under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the electronic disclosure and external-audit reporting system; copy retained in company records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit must be completed and reported before the annual general meeting of members; for a December 31 year-end, on or before March 31 of the following year, and within 90 days after fiscal year-end for other year-ends
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the company is a statutory audit target and fails to appoint an auditor or submit an audit report, administrative fines up to KRW 50,000,000 may be imposed on the representative officer, and the tax authority may disregard un-audited returns, impose unfaithful-return penalties, and extend the tax assessment period.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and payment, including the local income tax surcharge (10% of corporate tax) collected jointly
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) at the principal tax office; local income tax is collected by the NTS and transferred to the local government
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year-end, file by March 31 of the following year; for a non-calendar fiscal year-end, file within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or underpayment triggers additional tax of 20% (failure to file) or 10% (understated return) of the deficient corporate tax, plus daily delinquency charges of 0.025% per day until paid; prolonged delinquency may cause asset seizure, tax-office cancellation of business registration, and judicial dissolution as a dormant company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value Added Tax (VAT) semi-annual returns and payments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half (January 1 - June 30): file by July 25 of the same year; second half (July 1 - December 31): file by January 25 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 10% of the unpaid VAT for failure to file or underpayment, daily delinquency charges of 0.025% per day, and an extended 10-year reassessment period for fraudulent returns.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign investment change report and member transfer report for non-resident owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Designated foreign exchange bank or Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) on behalf of the Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days from the acquisition, transfer, or other reportable change of a membership interest in the Yuhan Hoesa; no fixed annual anniversary filing is required under the foreign-exchange framework
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report may incur administrative fines under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, loss of foreign-investment incentives, coercive correction orders, and adverse treatment during tax or AML inspections.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and its Enforcement Decree, an independent CPA audit is compulsory for: (i) companies listed on KOSPI, KOSDAQ, or KONEX; (ii) unlisted companies whose total assets at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year are at least KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 8.8 million); (iii) unlisted companies that exceed the small-company safe harbor comprising KRW 10 billion or more in annual turnover or 100 or more full-time employees; and (iv) banks, insurers, financial investment entities, and other public-interest corporations separately requiring external audit under their governing statutes. A Yuhan Hoesa that is unlicensed, unlisted, and remains below these asset, turnover, and headcount thresholds generally has no compulsory statutory audit, but foreign investors or lenders may contractually require a CPA-reviewed or audited financial statement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) apply to listed and public-interest corporations; non-listed small and medium-sized entities such as a typical Yuhan Hoesa may use Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) and the SME accounting standards issued by the Korean Accounting Standards Board. When an external audit is required, the engagement must follow Korean Standards on Auditing (KSA), which are aligned with International Standards on Auditing.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Republic of Korea does not require an annual UBO confirmation return to the court registry for a Yuhan Hoesa. Instead, anti-money-laundering customer due diligence rules require financial institutions to identify and verify beneficial owners when corporate bank accounts are opened and periodically thereafter. The company itself must continuously maintain a current register of members and must record any membership transfer without delay. For a foreign-invested Yuhan Hoesa, every acquisition or transfer of a membership interest by a non-resident must be reported to a designated foreign exchange bank or KOTRA within 30 days; there is no annual anniversary filing. The registers remain in the company's custody and are inspectable by tax officers, AML authorities, and court-appointed inspectors.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members and membership interest transfers
Register of Directors and Managing Officers
Minute Book of Members' Meetings and management resolutions
Commercial accounting books and supporting vouchers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - USD 2,000 per annum for a compliant local registered office and professional company-secretarial agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 15,000 per annum for a small non-listed Yuhan Hoesa; higher asset complexity, K-IFRS conversion, or dubbing/content localization revenue may push fees above USD 25,000 per annum

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 9% (base rate on taxable income up to KRW 200 million; effective 19% including 10% local income tax surtax for the first bracket; progressive CIT headline rates 9%, 19%, 21%, 24%, 27% for higher brackets; top effective rate 29.7% including local surtax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Foreign-investment tax reduction under Restriction of Special Taxation Act (RSTA); R&D tax credits; job creation tax credits; temporary investment tax credits; free-zone tax incentives limited to Foreign Investment Zones / Free Economic Zones; no general patent box regime; localization/translation services generally subject to standard rates without sector-specific exemption

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return Form No. 1 (법인세과세표준 및 세액계산서) via HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr); local income tax surtax filed on the same portal / WeTax
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; semi-annual intermediate prepayments required for fiscal years longer than 6 months; quarterly prepayments for prior-year taxable income over KRW 500 million
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months from the fiscal year-end (e.g., December 31 year-end filed by March 31); extension possible for justifiable cause; electronic filing mandatory for corporations above asset thresholds

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 10-digit Korean taxpayer ID for the Yuhan Hoesa
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be the Korean entity's own registration number; foreign parent ID cannot be substituted; electronic filing rejects mismatched IDs

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Corporate Name & Head Office Address
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered Korean legal name and domestic place of effective management
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If central management and control are in Korea, the company is a domestic corporation taxed on worldwide income; non-resident branch treatment not allowed

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business year commencement and closing dates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Short first fiscal year permitted but cannot exceed 12 months; transfer pricing documentation must align with the Korean fiscal year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income less allowable deductions, including expenses, depreciation, bad debts, and loss carryforwards
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All related-party transactions must be reported at arm's length; transfer pricing adjustments increase taxable income; foreign invoices must be substantively documented

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Applicable Tax Rates and Computed Tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Progressive CIT: 9% up to KRW 200M; 19% up to KRW 20B; 21% up to KRW 300B; 24% up to KRW 500B; 27% above KRW 500B; plus 10% local income tax surtax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Local surtax of 10% on national CIT applies even to foreign-owned Korean entities; treaty rate reductions do not reduce the Korean entity's own income tax

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit, R&D credits, job creation credits, foreign-investment tax reduction
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits limited to taxes paid by the Korean entity itself; localization services rarely qualify as R&D; foreign-investment incentives require prior government approval

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Intermediate prepayments and creditable withholding taxes on domestic income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If Korean clients withheld 3.3% service income tax, claim as credit; reconcile with HomeTax withholding ledger; do not credit foreign parent's taxes

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of all cross-border transactions with foreign related parties, including loans, services, intangibles, and management fees
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory regardless of amount; failure triggers penalties under LCITA Article 11; specify transfer pricing method and substantiate comparability

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 - Dividend, Interest, Royalty Payment Statements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Korean-source income paid to non-residents with WHT and DTA claim details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must identify beneficial owner, treaty article, TRC, and DTA relief documents; payer secondarily liable for any under-withholding

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: National CIT payable after credits and prepayments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Local income tax surtax filed separately; zero taxable income for a profitable-looking localization agency will trigger audit scrutiny

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty 20% of unpaid tax; under-reporting penalty 0.3% per day up to 10%; unjustified non-reporting 0.75% per day up to 10%; negligence penalty 10% (20% for intentional concealment); unfaithful return penalty 0.075% per day up to 7.5%; non-payment interest 1.2% per month; criminal tax evasion under Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 9: up to 5 years imprisonment or fine up to KRW 200 million

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national withholding plus 2% local income tax surtax = 24% effective aggregate on gross dividends; treaty reduction may apply (e.g., 5%–15% for qualified corporate shareholders under applicable DTA)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: File Non-Resident Tax Withholding and Reduction/Exemption Report with district tax office before payment via HomeTax; attach Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by foreign tax authority; Certificate of Beneficial Ownership proving no conduit arrangement; shareholding percentage and holding period evidence; detailed royalty/dividend/interest calculation; principal-purpose test (PPT) applies — substance required; if no prior approval, withhold full 24% and non-resident files refund claim
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory: 20% national + 2% local = 22% aggregate on interest and royalties; treaty rates commonly 0%–15% for interest and 10%–15% for royalties (e.g., Korea-US royalties 10%; Korea-UK 10%; Korea-Germany 15%); pure localization service fees not subject to withholding if services performed entirely outside Korea, but mixed contracts with IP licensing are recharacterized as royalties

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File mandatory when cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 5 billion annually; Master File required when MNE group consolidated revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion and Korean entity's related-party transactions exceed KRW 5 billion; simplified Local File may apply for small taxpayers; NTS may demand documentation for any transaction amount; failure to submit triggers penalty up to 30% of understated tax or KRW 300 million
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea applies substance-over-form GAAR under Framework Act on National Taxes Article 17 and LCITA Article 2; beneficial-ownership requirement and OECD BEPS principal-purpose test apply for DTA; passive shell entity without employees, premises, decision-making, or Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) will be recharacterized; CIGA for localization agency includes contract negotiation, quality control, dubbing production management, invoicing, and risk assumption — all must be substantiated in Korea

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure / Tax Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting intercompany service fees or filing CIT return without related-party transaction schedule to conceal non-arm's-length pricing; falsifying Local File or destroying contemporaneous documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unfaithful-return penalty up to 30% of understated tax under LCITA Article 11(4); negligence penalty 10%–20% under Framework Act Article 47-3; interest 1.2% per month; criminal evasion under Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 9: up to 5 years imprisonment or fine up to KRW 200 million
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate veil pierced where director signs false return or orders concealment; joint liability for tax and penalties; personal asset restitution including bank accounts, real estate, vehicles; NTS habitual delinquent blacklisting; travel ban and departure restriction; imprisonment up to 5 years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Failure on Outbound Dividends/Royalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, or royalties to non-resident parent without statutory 22%–24% withholding; claiming DTA relief without TRC and beneficial ownership documentation; misclassifying royalty payments as service fees
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Payer jointly and severally liable for uncollected WHT under CIT Act Article 114 and Framework Act Article 37; non-payment penalty 3% plus monthly interest 1.2%; false DTA claim penalty 10%–20%; criminal sanction up to 5 years imprisonment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Director executing wire transfer while avoiding WHT held personally liable for tax, penalties, and interest; de facto representative provision allows NTS to collect from personal assets; travel block and account freeze; embezzlement conviction if withheld taxes diverted, imprisonment 1–5 years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance and AML Facade
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating Yuhan Hoesa as invoice-splitting shell with no staff, no office, no operational control; using foreign payment rails (Wise/Payoneer) solely to avoid PE status; failing to register real-name beneficial owners with Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment up to 3 years or fine up to KRW 30 million under Financial Transactions Information Act; sham entity denied expense deductions; 40% unjustified-benefit penalty; commercial registry strike-off; foreign wire accounts suspended
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Director personally liable for corporate tax, local tax, and VAT where corporation is a facade; civil seizure of personal assets; blacklisting; imprisonment up to 5 years; travel ban and Interpol Yellow Notice upon flight
